In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
LDL from FH patients has a greater ability to stimulate SMC proliferation in culture than does LDL from normal subjects, and this action can be blocked by heparin or GAGs.
LDL from FH patients has the ability to alter the growth characteristics of SMC, an effect which may contribute to atherosclerotic lesion development in these patients.

LDL from FH subjects, in comparison to NL subjects, has the following effects: (1) increased ability to stimulate SMC proliferation; (2) increased ability to induce Ca2+ influx; (3) decreased net negative charge; (4) increased ability to increase cell membrane cholesterol; and (5) increased ability to inhibit LDL receptor activity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the effects of hypercholesteremia are mediated in part by LDL cholesterol, which may be regulated by the surface charge of LDL.
FH-LDL, by virtue of its increased cholesterol and reduced surface charge, can stimulate SMC proliferation.
